title: The Energy Bench
summary: Assemble charges and total the energy, carry a charge between points and turn a dipole in a field, tracking the work.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 2.7, Potential energy of a system of charges
concepts: Potential energy of a system of charges
Work to move a charge, W = q(V_B − V_A)
Potential energy of a dipole in a field
learningOutcome: The student can find the potential energy of a system of charges, the work to move a charge between two points, and the work to turn a dipole in a uniform field.

levels.title: Assemble the system
levels.adds: Baseline: the potential energy of a system is the work to bring the charges in one by one: add kq₁q₂/r over every pair (Example 2.4).
hints: Count each pair once: for three charges there are three pairs.
U = k(q₁q₂ + q₁q₃ + q₂q₃) / side for an equilateral triangle. Keep the signs.
Unlike charges attract, so bringing them together lowers the energy.

levels.title: Carry a charge
levels.adds: New idea: the work to carry a charge from A to B is q(V_B − V_A), and it does not depend on the route (Example 2.5).
hints: Find the potential at A and at B from the fixed charges: V = Σ kq/r.
W = q₀(V_B − V_A) is the work done by the outside agent. Watch the sign of q₀.
The force is conservative: any route gives the same work.

levels.title: Turn the dipole
levels.adds: New idea: a dipole’s energy in a field is U = −pE cos θ, and turning it costs the change in U (Example 2.6).
hints: U = −pE cos θ. Work for the agent = U(final) − U(initial).
U is lowest at θ = 0° and highest at θ = 180°, so turning towards the field gives negative work.
p = q × 2a in coulomb-metres, E in N/C, so U is in joules.

misconceptions: The energy of a system is the sum of kq/r for every charge on its own
A longer route takes more work in an electrostatic field
A dipole has its highest energy along the field
Each pair of charges is counted twice
